To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the psychosocial sequelae of first trimester vacuum aspiration termination of pregnancy are few in number, mild, and transient, and that the procedure is associated with a significant improvement in psychosocial well-being.

women who undergo termination by vacuum aspiration are likely to be relieved of the distress associated with an unwanted pregnancy, and are likely to experience improvement in their psychosocial adjustment, with few adverse sequelae.

termination of pregnancy is a relatively safe and effective procedure that, if carried out in the first trimester of pregnancy, does not have serious psychosocial consequences for the majority of patients.

the psychosocial consequences of termination of pregnancy.
the psychosocial consequences of termination of pregnancy by vacuum aspiration, with special reference to the role of counselling.
the psychosocial effects of therapeutic abortion, and in particular the extent to which women who undergo abortion experience adverse psychiatric and social sequelæ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the majority of women who undergo termination of pregnancy in the first trimester experience a marked improvement in their psychosocial adjustment, and that the procedure does not have any significant adverse effects.
termination of pregnancy by vacuum aspiration, with brief preoperative counselling, is a safe procedure, and that the majority of patients experience no significant psychosocial sequelae.

the psychological and social consequences of termination of early pregnancy, in the hands of a competent team, are negligible, provided that adequate counselling is given to the patient beforehand and adequate support provided after termination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the psychosocial consequences of termination of pregnancy by vacuum aspiration are minimal and favourable.
the majority of patients were not only free of adverse sequelae but had made significant psychosocial improvements.
termination of pregnancy by vacuum aspiration is a safe, effective, and psychologically acceptable procedure.
